Stepwise selection of terms

Source: R/inference.R
step_regcomp.Rd

Forward, backward or bidirectional selection of the terms of one distribution parameter's formula by AIC or BIC, as in stats::step() and StepReg. Selection makes the reported standard errors, intervals and p values of the final model too optimistic (Harrell 2015, sec. 4.3); prefer penalized estimation (see penalty()) or cross validation for prediction, and treat stepwise results as exploratory.

Usage

step_regcomp(
  object,
  scope = NULL,
  direction = c("both", "backward", "forward"),
  criterion = c("AIC", "BIC", "AICc", "HQ"),
  par = NULL,
  trace = FALSE
)

Arguments

object

A frequentist fit: the starting model.

scope

A one sided formula with the largest set of terms considered for par; by default the terms of the starting model (backward only).

direction

"both", "backward" or "forward".

criterion

"AIC", "BIC", "AICc" (small sample AIC) or "HQ" (Hannan-Quinn).

par

Distribution parameter whose formula is searched; the main one by default. Random effect terms are kept.

trace

Print each step.

Value

The selected fit, with the path of steps in attr(, "steps").

Examples

d <- data.frame(x1 = rnorm(200), x2 = rnorm(200), x3 = rnorm(200))
d$y <- rpois(200, exp(0.5 + 0.4 * d$x1))
f0 <- regcomp(y ~ 1, family = "poisson", data = d)
fs <- step_regcomp(f0, scope = ~ x1 + x2 + x3, direction = "forward", criterion = "BIC")
formula(fs)
#> $lambda
#> y ~ x1
#> <environment: 0x560d7330d088>
#> 
#> attr(,"given")
#> [1] "lambda"
attr(fs, "steps")
#>       step      BIC
#> 1    start 660.1694
#> + x1  + x1 631.6967
